instruction: Explain overfitting in machine learning to a high school student in simple terms.
response_a: Overfitting is when a model learns the details of the training data too well, and it starts to make mistakes on new or unseen data. This happens because the model has been trained on only a small amount of information from the training set, which means that it doesn't have enough experience to generalize well to new situations. As a result, the model may not be able to predict outcomes accurately for new data. Overfitting can lead to poor performance on both accuracy and generalization.
response_b: Overfitting is when a model learns the details of the training data too well, and it starts to make mistakes on new or unseen data. It's like trying to draw a picture with only one pencil - you'll end up drawing an exact copy of your friend's drawing, not something that looks like their original. Overfitting can happen when a model has been trained on too much data, which means it's learned patterns from all the data rather than just the ones that were used for training. This can lead to poor performance on new data, as the model doesn't generalize well to new situations. To avoid overfitting, we need to use more data and try different models until we find one that works best.
